Plant height and biomass models from GOBI LiDAR + VNIR — Muresk and AGT NUE trials 2025

Built 2026-10-06. Features: LiDAR360-style preprocessing (outlier removal, plot-local ground, canopy classification, canopy-only metrics) and cleaned VNIR (clipped bands masked, adaptive soil mask, per-pixel indices). Validation: nested repeated 10-fold CV (feature selection inside each fold), LOOCV for the top height models, leave-one-flight-out and cross-trial transfer.

Erratum, 9 October 2026

Added after a plot-level audit of every per-plot VNIR file against its original orthomosaic (ENVI 6.2, all 172 bands, all flights) and an independent recomputation of the VNIR v3 features. The original report is kept unchanged as REPORT_height_biomass_2026-10-06_original_2026-10-06.html.

  1. AGT 2025-11-13 (maturity), both flights: the VNIR orthomosaics are at-sensor radiance, not reflectance (float32, no reflectance scale factor, values 5 to 40, oxygen absorption visible at 760 nm, NDVI between -0.04 and 0.04 in every one of the 969 plots). Every AGT maturity VNIR feature is therefore invalid. The agt_maturity VNIR_core, Fused_core and Fused_all rows in section 3 and the agt_maturity two_stream and vnir_only rows in section 4 are withdrawn. AGT maturity is a LiDAR-only dataset until the cubes are reprocessed to reflectance.
  2. AGT 2025-09-22 (anthesis): the 670 nm band is clipped to zero on 16 to 75% of plot pixels (median 48%), so "valid on most pixels" applies to Muresk only. Indices that use a 620 to 690 nm band (NDVI, OSAVI, kNDVI, NIRv, WDRVI, MTCI, LCI, REP, refl_R, red_depth and their x cover / x H95 products) track the clipped share (r up to 0.65) rather than the crop. The agt_anthesis VNIR_core and fused results should be re-run without those features before they are quoted. Under a strict filter, 113 of the 252 ground-truth plots have a usable red band.
  3. Extraction quality: all per-plot VNIR files (Muresk 128 + 128, AGT 816 + 741 + 228) are pixel-exact copies of their cubes in every band and sit exactly on the cube grid, except AGT 2025-11-13 flight 2 plots 1001 and 1024, which lost 4 and 1 edge pixels to a rounding defect in the writer (fixed in PhenoApp v3.0.1). Pixel-count shortfalls elsewhere are holes in the orthomosaics, not extraction losses.
  4. Unchanged: all LiDAR results and the Muresk biomass results (section 3). Note that the "acc" column (100 - MAPE) reflects the spread of biomass values, not model skill, and should not be read as accuracy where R² is near zero.

Erratum 2, 10 October 2026: height on the anthesis flight

  1. Muresk has one ruler height per plot, measured at maturity (2025-11-21). The "2025-09-30 (anthesis)" height rows in section 2 compared anthesis-flight features with that maturity ruler; no height was measured at anthesis. Those rows (and the leave-flight-out height transfer) are withdrawn as error metrics. Height RMSE / R² are valid for the maturity flight only: linear calibration on cth_p95 LOOCV R² 0.23 / RMSE 4.5 cm; best model (LiDAR + VNIR joint PCA, ridge, 9 Oct rebuild) R² 0.55 / 3.4 cm.
  2. The canopy had not reached its final height at the anthesis flight: the LiDAR canopy-top P95 is 10.2 cm (sd 4.6) higher at maturity than at anthesis, and the LiDAR-only maturity model applied to the anthesis flight predicts 71.8 cm against the 84.7 cm ruler at maturity (difference 12.9 cm, sd 4.5). The anthesis flight is therefore reported as a predicted height with the maturity-minus-anthesis difference (rebuild of 9-10 October 2026, section 3), never as an error score. The anthesis-flight LiDAR still ranks the plots' final height well (r 0.70 with the maturity ruler), which is what the earlier agreement numbers measured.
  3. The height ground-truth column has been removed from the anthesis-flight tables of the 9 October dataset so that it cannot be mistaken for an anthesis measurement.

Valid-plot lists per flight: <flight folder>\vnir_qc_2026-10-08\valid_plots_for_modeling_*.csv (Muresk anthesis 128, Muresk maturity 126, AGT anthesis 113 of 252 ground-truth plots, AGT maturity 0); summary in Biomass Experiment\2025-09-30\vnir_qc_2026-10-08\plot_filter_summary.csv. Tool fixes (edge-pixel loss, uint16 truncation of float cubes, flight-level reflectance check, red-clipping censoring, QC applied to fused families) are logged in the PhenoApp v3 README as v3.0.1.

Every per-plot LAS holds exactly the points of the whole cloud inside its polygon (count match 128/128 on both flights, 100% inside, no noise points above the canopy, valid headers by lasinfo). The Ouster cloud is single-return (multi-return fraction 0), so gap fraction is estimated from ground-level returns, not from return counts; point format 3 carries intensity and GPS time, classification is all 0 (ground is classified here by the plot-local plane).

Correction (2026-10-09): the table above shows agt_2025-11-13 flight 1 passing QC on 747 plots only because the QC checked coverage and vegetation fraction; the cube is radiance, not reflectance, and none of its VNIR values are usable (see erratum). For agt_2025-09-22 the 670 nm band is valid on a median of 47% of plot pixels (range 16 to 75%), so the statement below that 670 nm is valid "on most" pixels holds for Muresk only. PhenoApp v3.0.1 adds a flight-level reflectance check and sets red-based indices to NaN on red-clipped plots.

Per-plot VNIR files are bit-exact copies of the orthomosaic (verified over all bands). The GRYFN cube clips negative reflectance to 0: the 470 nm band is valid on a minority of canopy pixels and 670 nm on most; indices use only pixels where every input band is valid, and the vegetation fraction uses an adaptive NDVI threshold per flight (0.50 at anthesis, 0.18 on the senesced maturity canopy).
